owner_and_capability: People Directory student profiles, School Membership lifecycle and Care Plan student care; retire rollback-only storage without changing public student identity.
atomic_cutover: Migration 1.15.399 replaces the stored visit-count function and drops compatibility objects atomically on ordinary upgrades and fresh replays. Deployment stops both application services and verifies the complete release backup first. Live integrity and dependency checks run before deployment and under DDL locks. Historical compatibility counters, observation windows and operator evidence documents are not deployment gates.
tests: Entire backend suite passed after Contract registration and stored-function correction; affected packages also passed with -count=1. See docs/operations/student-owner-storage-contract.md.

Contract tests cover a populated ordinary upgrade with 566 historical reads and 12 writes, unchanged owner and history snapshots, object removal and function replacement, unknown dependencies, integrity failures, lock timeout, transactional rollback, irreversible Down refusal and empty initial replay.

Real pg_dump/pg_restore of a synthetic pre-Contract database preserved all measured row hashes, enabled/forced RLS and validated owner FKs. The actual prior server image ed76e883668985014427f8cd860e1fe7efb24ed0 then started against it and returned HTTP 200 on localhost health; post-start fingerprints remained identical.
Release backup and deployment boundary tests cover preflight, application stop, backup-before-migration ordering and full rollback without operator evidence files.

runtime_evidence.source: Local observations on 2026-09-20, PostgreSQL 17.11 aarch64. No production writes. Sources distinguish durable synthetic measurements from the earlier shared-test-server lock observation. These are historical core and recovery observations, not new measurements of the revised deployment policy.
runtime_evidence.workload: One ungated Contract core execution on 1448 synthetic profiles across 12 populated schools, 2830 status days and 16 current sick flags, with fsync/synchronous_commit/full_page_writes on. Separately, deletion preview and execute each have 30 sequential samples after five warmups against the contracted schema on that durable local server. Lock-blocking observations use the shared local test server as documented. These are not a production-data clone or evidence of an observed school day.
runtime_evidence.thresholds: Require unchanged owner/history snapshots, no unexpected errors, and no retirement when live integrity or compatibility-hit checks fail. Contract has a 60-second context deadline and 5-second lock timeout. The user revised the mandatory observation-window policy on 2026-09-20: ordinary deployments need no evidence file or waiting period. Explicitly supplied historical evidence retains its strict window and freshness validation. API latency is descriptive; no production latency ceiling is claimed.

affected_rows.result: Contract preserved 1448 profiles, memberships and Care Plan rows, 2830 status-day rows, and 16 sick flags with timestamps; complete before/after owner/history JSON snapshots matched. The three retired relations were absent.

query_count.result: Contract core: 26 BUN query events, including multi-statement batches as single events, not 26 PostgreSQL substatements. Deletion preview: 22 events per sample; execute: 54 per sample, each across 30 measured samples.

latency_p50.result: Nearest-rank p50 across 30 post-warmup samples: deletion preview 4.011958 ms; execute 10.458625 ms. Local sequential workload, not production tail latency.

latency_p95.result: Nearest-rank p95 across 30 post-warmup samples: deletion preview 4.82925 ms; execute 12.717 ms.

errors.result: The durable Contract run and all 60 measured deletion operations completed without unexpected errors. Expected lock-timeout and invalid-evidence failures are asserted separately.

pool_wait.result: Contract DBStats WaitCount/WaitDuration deltas were 0/0s. Both deletion sample sets recorded aggregate pool wait count 0 and duration 0 ms.

lock_wait.result: PostgreSQL wait_event_type=Lock and pg_blocking_pids observed the intended blocker: released case lower bound 154.161750 ms, total 198.636708 ms; timeout case lower bound 154.130959 ms, total 5.015356417 s. These are sampled lower bounds, not SQL-duration proxies. Raw source records the earlier shared-server run.

deadlocks.result: Durable Contract database deadlock counters were 0 before and 0 after; deletion workload counter delta was 0. Short-run statistics observations, not a prediction under production concurrency.

job_duration.result: Single durable synthetic Contract core run after the SHA-256 correction: 105.311875 ms. Fixture setup and assertions excluded. This does not measure the production deployment's backup, preflight or image startup.

job_retries.reason: Contract is a synchronous one-shot migration, not a retrying background worker. A lock timeout aborts; operator rerun requires fresh checks. There is no job retry queue to measure.

job_backlog.reason: Contract is a synchronous migration with no background copy backlog. Historical compatibility usage is diagnostic, not a release gate.

failure.result: Induced blocker caused PostgreSQL lock timeout after 5.015356417 s; the test verified current snapshots and both rollback relations remained. Unknown stored-function dependency regression first reproduced silent acceptance, then passed with preflight refusal.

rollback.result: Failed Contract transactions preserved owner/history snapshots and rollback relations. Separately, the real 1827589-byte pre-Contract custom-format dump restored successfully into template0; six table SHA-256 fingerprints matched exactly, owner RLS and eight validated FKs survived, and the rollback view returned 1448 rows. The actual prior server image then started with local generated credentials against the restore, returned localhost health HTTP 200, and left all measured fingerprints unchanged. This is a backend startup smoke, not an authenticated school-day or frontend restore test.

smoke.result: Full backend suite passed on the contracted default template after fixing the SQL-function dependency. The affected api/students, services/users, presence service and studentintegration packages passed uncached; raw repeated deletion workflow evidence also passed on durable PostgreSQL.

rollback_and_cleanup: No automatic Down reconstructs removed archive data. Normal deployment stops application writers, creates and verifies a complete pre-migration release-backup bundle, and restores it with the matching prior images on failure. Direct migration commands do not stop services or create backups. The observation-window evidence subsystem and absolute-zero-counter gate are removed.
exit_criterion: Old storage and compatibility objects are removed, owner rows remain unchanged, and the stored deletion-count function uses owner tables. Relevant tests and architecture checks pass. Deploy staging before promoting the tested release to production through the normal backup/rollback pipeline; this code change is not a deployment execution.
